items.title: The crisis after the flood in Assam villages: Lost livestock, missed crop, and wait for aid
items.summary: When the floodwaters rose around their home in Rajapul on July 19, Bandana Buragohain had no way of getting out on her own. The 70-year-old clung to the back of a man from her village as he waded into the current. At one point, the force of the water pushed him backwards. A couple of other boys came and helped carry her to a nearby house with a terrace, where around 30 others had already taken shelter. “I somehow managed to stay alive. I could have died,” she recalled. Rajapul, in the Nazira subdivision of Sivasagar district, was among the areas caught in the path of what several reports have described as one of Assam's worst localised floods since the 1950s. After days of heavy rain across the region, including 137 mm recorded over eight to nine hours in the neighbouring hills of Nagaland , a sudden rush of water moved downstream into the plains on July 19, sending the Dikhow, Disang and Janji, rivers that eventually meet the Brahmaputra, above extreme flood levels within hours and engulfing settlements before families could evacuate. items.title: Litigant in Kerala attacks parents of lawyers who represented his wife
items.summary: Parents of two lawyer-siblings in Kerala were attacked by a litigant on Thursday night as retaliation for appearing against him in a case filed by his wife. According to a first information report lodged by the police, two men attacked the parents. The FIR was registered based on a complaint filed by the advocates' 79-year-old mother from the hospital where she was being treated after the attack. Her 80-year-old husband, the advocates' father, was stabbed repeatedly and he remains in critical condition. According to the FIR, the advocates represented the wife of one of the attackers who sought police protection from him due to domestic dispute. At around 5:30 pm on August 13, two men, including the irate litigant, forcefully entered the house of the advocate's parents and asked them where their son was. According to the FIR, the men were armed with knives and threatened to kill the advocates and their parents. When the advocates' mother asked them to leave, the attackers dragged the father out of the house, threw him on the ground, attempted to slit his throat and repeatedly stabbed him in the torso.
